license.notes: Minted 2026-09-16 by tools/new_species.py from 'desk' and shaped the same day. REFERENCE: 1990s panel-system office (Herman Miller Action Office / Steelcase 9000): fabric-covered acoustic screens 1.2-1.7 m tall on levelling feet, painted steel frame with a top trim cap; work surfaces cantilevered off the panel rails at 0.74 m; a 0.42 m drawer pedestal under each; an overhead binder bin on the spine panel where the panel is tall enough to carry one; pods back to back in rows with a circulation aisle between them.

notes: WHY THIS SPECIES EXISTS. Ten volumes in the library carry `cubicle` in their name -- `cubicles_w_0` .. `cubicles_e_2` in `office` and `office_stepped`, every one 8.0 x 6.0 x 1.2 m -- and every one of them was routed to `desk`, whose genome takes width to 12 and depth to 6, so it FIT and built as desk geometry at that size: four 8 m work surfaces butted edge to edge over 6 m of depth (`desk.py`'s `row_max` rows), a raft with no aisle. The walker, cold run 9060, standing 2.68 m from `cubicles_w_0_col`: "these desks are too close to each other?". A cubicle bank is not a desk: it is rows of workstations inside 1.2-1.5 m partition screens with an aisle between the rows. `desk` keeps desks. RANGES: width from 2.0 (one bay plus its cross screens) to 16.0; depth from 1.6 (one pod band: a spine screen, a 0.75 m surface and a knee) to 12.0; height 1.0 to 2.0, which is the panel range the reference covers -- below 1.0 it is a bench, above 2.0 it is a partition wall and Deli Counter has partitions. AISLE: `aisle_min` 1.1 is Deli Counter's `agent_contract.clearances.min_corridor_width_m` read 2026-09-16, itself `2 * nav_bake.agent_radius_m (0.4) + 0.3` body margin -- so a bank wide enough for two bands carries an aisle this pipeline's own body fits down, and one that is not stays a single band rather than shipping an aisle nobody can use.
